title: Closed pushforward preserves module cokernels
statement: Let $i:Z\to X$ be a closed immersion of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-closed-immersion]. For arbitrary $\mathcal O_Z$-module sheaves $A,B$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and a morphism $f:A\to B$, the module pushforward $i_*$ [def-pc-module-pullback] preserves its cokernel [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]: the pushforward of $B\to\operatorname{coker}(f)$ is a cokernel of $i_*f$. Equivalently, $i_*$ preserves the colimit of the parallel pair $(f,0)$. There is no quasi-coherence hypothesis and no choice of ideal.

proof.text: At x=i(z), the three pushed stalks of an exact short complex are isomorphic to the original three abelian stalks. Naturality of the closed-pushforward stalk comparison gives an isomorphism of short complexes. The original stalk complex is exact, since abelian sheaf stalks preserve finite limits and colimits.
